blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
The most reliable way to predict future behaviour is to look at past behaviour. That is the idea behind behavioural interviews. Instead of asking "Are you a team player?", a good interviewer asks "Tell me about a time when your team disagreed on a decision. What did you do?" The candidate cannot give a theoretical answer — they have to tell a real story.

A useful framework is STAR: Situation, Task, Action, Result. It helps candidates structure their answers and interviewers compare them fairly. When every candidate is assessed against the same competencies, personal impressions matter less and the evidence matters more.

Done well, behavioural interviews are the fairest way to hire, because everyone is judged on how they actually behaved, not on how well they describe themselves. The interviewer's job is to probe until the real result appears — because that is where a rehearsed answer usually falls apart.

items.q: According to the text, what is the core idea behind behavioural interviews?
options: Team players are the best hires
Past behaviour is the most reliable predictor of future behaviour
items.why: "The most reliable way to predict future behaviour is to look at past behaviour."

items.q: What does the STAR framework stand for?
items.why: "A useful framework is STAR: Situation, Task, Action, Result."

items.q: Why does the interviewer keep probing for the real result?
options: Because that is where a rehearsed answer usually falls apart
To make the interview last longer
To avoid asking about the situation
items.why: "probe until the real result appears — because that is where a rehearsed answer usually falls apart."

items.q: Which statement would the author most likely DISAGREE with?
options: A candidate who sounds confident should be hired on that basis alone
Asking about a specific past event reveals more than a general question
The same competencies should be used to compare candidates
A real story is harder to fake than a theory
items.why: Inferência: o texto defende avaliar pelo comportamento real, não pela forma como o candidato se descreve.

items.q: The text suggests that a structured framework like STAR mainly helps because it…
options: removes the need for follow-up questions
lets interviewers compare people on the same basis
items.why: Inferência: "It helps… interviewers compare them fairly" e reduz o peso das impressões pessoais.

blocks.instruction: Ouça Oliver conduzindo uma entrevista comportamental. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
Thanks for coming in. This is a commercial role, so I'm going to ask you to walk me through some real situations rather than talk in general terms. Take your time.

Tell me about a time when a negotiation was going badly and you had to turn it around. I want the specific deal — what the situation was, what your task was, exactly what you did, and how it ended.

Good. So while your manager was still pushing for the original price, you were quietly building a second option for the client. That's helpful. Now, you said the client "came round in the end" — that's a little vague for me. What was the actual outcome? By how much did the margin move?

I ask because a strong answer always has a clear result at the end. When someone can only describe the situation and the action, but the outcome stays fuzzy, that's a bit of a red flag for me. I'm not doubting you — I just like to probe. So, precise numbers if you can: what did the deal close at, and what did you learn from it?
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: What does Oliver ask the candidate to do at the start?
options: Describe their strengths in general terms
Walk him through real situations rather than talk in general
items.why: "walk me through some real situations rather than talk in general terms."

items.q: According to Oliver, what was the candidate doing while the manager pushed for the original price?
options: Quietly building a second option for the client
items.why: "while your manager was still pushing for the original price, you were quietly building a second option."

items.q: Why does Oliver push back on the phrase "came round in the end"?
options: It is too vague and has no clear result
He wants to end the interview
items.why: "that's a little vague for me. What was the actual outcome?" — falta o resultado concreto.

items.q: What does Oliver consider a "red flag"?
options: When the candidate asks about the salary
When a candidate speaks too fast
When the situation and action are clear but the outcome stays fuzzy
items.why: Inferência: para ele, uma boa resposta STAR precisa terminar com resultado claro.

items.q: How would you best describe Oliver's approach?
options: Fair but insistent on a concrete result
Hostile and trying to catch the candidate out
items.why: Inferência: "I'm not doubting you — I just like to probe" — firme, mas justo.

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "We use a structured interview so every candidate faces the same questions." A structured interview is one that…
options: follows the same fixed questions and criteria for everyone
changes freely depending on the candidate
is conducted only by senior managers
items.why: Structured interview = entrevista estruturada: mesmas perguntas e critérios para todos, o que a torna comparável.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "A structured process helps reduce unconscious ___ when we compare candidates."
items.why: Bias = viés; o objetivo da estrutura é reduzir o viés inconsciente.

items.q: "When a candidate's story has no numbers and no result, that's a red flag." A red flag is…
options: a warning sign that something may be wrong
a strong point in their favour
items.why: Red flag = sinal de alerta, algo que acende a luz amarela.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "Good interviewers ___ for detail until the real result appears."
items.why: To probe = aprofundar, cavar detalhes com perguntas de acompanhamento.

items.q: "We hire against a clear competency framework." A competency is best described as…
options: a specific skill or ability the role requires
items.why: Competency = competência: uma habilidade específica que o cargo exige e que se avalia na entrevista.

blocks.instruction: Expressões que aparecem em entrevistas e processos de contratação. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "Before we make an offer, the head of desk has to sign off on it." To sign off on means to…
items.why: Sign off on = aprovar formalmente, dar o aval final.

items.q: "Can you walk me through exactly what you did next?" To walk someone through means to…
items.why: Walk me through = me guiar passo a passo pela situação.

items.q: "Her answer was vague, so I had to dig deeper." To dig deeper means to…
options: move on to the next topic
ask more questions to get below the surface
accept the answer as it is
items.why: Dig deeper = ir mais fundo, buscar detalhes que não apareceram na resposta inicial.

items.q: "He described the plan but never followed through." This means he…
options: failed to carry it to completion
items.why: Follow through = levar até o fim o que foi combinado.

items.q: "That vague result really raised a red flag for me." This means it…
options: signalled a possible problem worth checking
confirmed she was the best candidate
made no difference to the decision
items.why: Raise a red flag = acender um alerta, sinalizar algo que merece ser investigado.
